channel.title: World
channel.description: The Washington Post World section provides information and analysis of breaking world news stories. In addition to our world news and video, Post World News offers discussions and blogs on major international news and economic issues.

item.title: U.S. intervened in criminal probe of oilman helping Trump in Venezuela
item.dc:creator: Samuel Oakford, Samantha Schmidt, Anthony Faiola, Karen DeYoung
item.description: Swiss prosecutors asked the U.S. Justice Department to arrest Alejandro Betancourt. Instead, he was given a multi-entry visa and allowed to travel to the United States.

item.title: Rescuers race to find survivors after Himalayan floods kill at least 270
item.dc:creator: Aoife Walsh
item.description: Hundreds of people, including more than 640 tourists, remain missing after the floods hit the Nepal-China border.

item.title: She made history as a trans Indigenous chief. Then addiction cost her the job.
item.dc:creator: Marina Dias, Dan Agostini
item.description: Majur Traytowu is struggling to hold on to influence and authority amid a devastating alcohol epidemic ravaging her territory — and her own life.

item.title: Iran weighs harsh penalties for contact with outside media in ‘foreign influence’ bill
item.dc:creator: Sammy Westfall
item.description: The push comes nearly six months after the U.S. and Israel launched the war, with no immediate diplomatic breakthrough in sight.

item.title: Yayoi Kusama, whose art evoked hallucinatory wonder, dies at 97
item.dc:creator: Juno Carmel
item.description: Her hypnotic, unconventional works propelled her from near-obscurity to a place in the world’s most prominent museums.

item.title: Canada, pressured by Trump, wants new trade partners. Here’s why it’s hard.
item.dc:creator: Sammy Westfall
item.description: The country needs infrastructure and deals to expand exports beyond the United States.

item.title: Scores dead, hundreds missing in flash floods on Nepal-China border
item.dc:creator: Joshua Yang
item.description: An avalanche caused the Bhotekoshi River to overflow, sending waves of water and mud that swept buildings and people away.

item.title: Europe eyes Russia in attacks on weapons and cargo. But Germany treads lightly.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Belton, Anthony Faiola
item.description: European security officials officials said an explosive drone found at Leipzig/Halle airport in Germany fits a pattern of likely Russian aggression across Europe.

item.title: Prince Harry and Meghan are back in the U.K.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Craw
item.description: The couple shocked Britain's royal watchers last week with the news they would return to live in the U.K., ending a self-imposed exile in California.

item.title: CIA director’s secretive visit to Moscow stirs mystery
item.dc:creator: Alex Horton, Michael Birnbaum, Warren Strobel, Joyce Lee
item.description: A Kremlin spokesman said John Ratcliffe did not meet with Vladimir Putin and that it was "premature" to say whether the trip would affect fraught U.S.-Russia relations.

item.title: Fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record threatens to become worst in history
item.dc:creator: Rael Ombuor, Rachel Chason
item.description: The response to Congo’s raging Ebola epidemic has been hampered by a severe lack of funding and pervasive misinformation, according to people on the front lines.

item.title: Canada announces retaliatory tariffs on U.S. products as trade war deepens
item.dc:creator: Riley Beggin
item.description: Canada announced new tariffs of up to 50 percent on hundreds of American goods in retaliation for U.S. tariffs that took effect last week. Starting Sept. 8, Canada will double tariffs on American steel and aluminum to 50 percent and impose tariffs on around 700 other products.

item.title: The U.S. and Canada are in a trade war. China aims to win it.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Yang
item.description: Beijing, seeking an advantage, casts itself as a global champion of free trade.

item.title: The U.S. is escalating its economic war on Iran. Here’s what that means.
item.dc:creator: Sammy Westfall, Joshua Yang
item.description: Iran’s top trade partners include China, Iraq, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates. But the Trump administration has not said who new sanctions would target, or how so.

item.title: Trump says U.S. could rename Lake Ontario as Lake America amid Canada trade war
item.dc:creator: Sammy Westfall
item.description: The president cited his tariff fight in a social media post, saying the United States doesn’t expect to be “doing much business with Ontario any longer.”
